subject: DI05007011

intro_text.en: English-only,diagram-focused Unit 1:computer development/types,PC functional blocks,CPU/board/memory/storage/I/O/power,hardware/software/firmware,BIOS/UEFI/CMOS,laptop components,ports/connectors and dated specifications. Four executed software helpers support worksheets;physical Practicals1/4 are guided only,not fabricated hardware/electrical/BIOS work. Original practice marks are suggested,not official GTU allocations.

h.en: 1.1 Computer systems,IPO and PC development

body.en:
A computer system accepts input, processes instructions/data, retains working/persistent information and produces output. Hardware, software,firmware and the user’s task work together; a system is not only its CPU.

  • Personal computers brought programmable computing to individual users. IBM introduced the IBM 5150 Personal Computer in August 1981; it was an influential PC standard, not the first personal computer ever.
  • PC development includes more integration, memory/storage capacity, graphical/networked use, portable systems and specialized workloads. Do not assume each new generation is faster for every task merely from clock speed.
  • A desktop may use separate display/keyboard/power components; a laptop integrates many into one portable device. Form factor and integration affect servicing and upgrade options.
  • This unit identifies roles and interfaces. Detailed 8085 architecture/buses belong to Unit 2; detailed memory/storage to Unit 3; peripheral working principles to Unit 4 and troubleshooting/assembly to Unit 5.

h.en: 1.2 Types of computers:use,scale and deployment are different axes

body.en:
Syllabus typeIdea / example contextImportant distinction
MicrocomputerPersonal computing built around microprocessor-based processing;desktop/laptop examples.A workstation can also be a microcomputer;categories may overlap.
MinicomputerHistorical midrange/multiuser computer category.Not the same as a modern small-form-factor miniPC or a product named Mac mini.
MainframeEnterprise multiuser/transaction and reliability-oriented computing.Not defined simply as a physically large box or the fastest scientific computer.
SupercomputerLarge-scale parallel/high-performance computing for suitable computational workloads.Application/workload and architecture matter,not just cabinet size.
WorkstationProfessional/technical personal system for suitable engineering/creative/scientific work.A role/capability category,not automatically a separate size tier.
CloudAccess/deployment model for remotely provided computing resources/services.Uses underlying physical hardware;not a single CPU class or a replacement for all local devices.
Embedded systemComputing integrated into a device for particular functions.May use a microcontroller/SoC and need not look like a desktop or run a general-purpose desktop OS.

Do not arrange every row as one mutually exclusive “smallest to largest” ladder. A cloud-hosted resource can use server-class hardware,and a professional workstation can have a desktop form factor.

title.en: 2. PC Block Diagram and Core Components

h.en: 2.1 The PC block diagram

body.en:
Read the diagram as functional relationships,not an exact wiring/pinout or a measured board. Input devices supply data/control; CPU executes operations; RAM holds active working state; persistent storage retains programs/files; output devices present results.

  • The motherboard/interconnects allow components to communicate;device controllers and firmware/OS software also participate.
  • Storage data is typically brought into working memory when used. RAM and a storage drive are different resources.
  • Power delivery supports the components,not the logical data path. A CPU alone cannot supply power,display a result or store every persistent file.
  • Modern integration varies:memory controllers,graphics or other functions may share a CPU/SoC package. The conceptual blocks need not be separate removable chips.

h.en: 2.2 CPU:ALU,Control Unit and internal state

body.en:
The central processing unit (CPU) executes instructions. A simplified teaching view includes:

PartRole
Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)Performs relevant arithmetic and logical operations under the instruction/control design.
Control Unit (CU)Coordinates instruction/control sequencing and signals needed for operations.
Registers/internal stateFast internal storage used while executing instructions;not the same as the installed RAM capacity.

Fetch/decode/execute is a useful simplified cycle,not a complete description of every modern pipeline. A core count,clock number or brand name alone is not a universal performance score. The ALU/CU are functional parts of processing,not parts a student removes from a CPU package.

h.en: 2.3 Motherboard and component interconnection

body.en:
The motherboard / system board is the main circuit board interconnecting/supporting system components. A typical modular desktop may expose a CPU socket,RAM slots,firmware storage,expansion connectors,storage interfaces,power connectors and rear/front-I/O connections.

  • Actual layouts differ by model/form factor. Do not identify a connector solely by approximate position in a generic drawing.
  • A laptop/compact system may integrate/solder CPU or memory instead of offering ordinary desktop sockets/slots. Do not assume a component is removable or upgradeable.
  • A chipset/controller supports relevant I/O/connectivity;historical northbridge/southbridge and bus details are studied in Unit 2. Modern integration does not always follow that old two-chip layout.
  • Our labelled board drawing is a schematic role map,not a photograph,service manual or proof that an actual motherboard was handled.

h.en: 2.4 RAM,ROM and persistent HDD/SSD storage

body.en:
ComponentPurposePersistence / common trap
RAMActive program/data workspace.Ordinary system RAM is volatile;power-off loses its active contents. More RAM is not more SSD capacity.
ROM/nonvolatile firmware storageRetain suitable low-level code/data.ROM is a historical/read-only category;modern firmware often resides in updateable flash. Do not conclude all firmware can never change.
HDDPersistent storage using rotating magnetic media and mechanisms.Not the same working resource as RAM;internal mechanisms are not opened in this exercise.
SSDPersistent solid-state storage,commonly flash-based.SSDs have different interfaces/form factors;not every SSD is NVMe or an interchangeable module.

SATA and NVMe are not synonyms;M.2 is a form-factor/connector family rather than a guarantee of one protocol. A common M.2 NVMe module plugs into a suitable slot instead of needing a SATA-style data cable. RAID describes a storage arrangement,not an interface. These distinctions are developed further in Units2/3.

h.en: 2.5 Keyboard,mouse and monitor as system I/O

body.en:
A keyboard supplies key events; a mouse/pointing device supplies pointing/button information. The device/controller and OS interpret those inputs;an unresponsive app is not automatically proof of a broken peripheral.

A monitor/display presents visual output through an appropriate graphics/display path. In common PC terminology,an “LED monitor” is often an LED-backlit LCD,not automatically a direct-emissive LED or OLED panel. LCD/LED construction/operation is studied in Unit 4.

  • A desktop may require external keyboard/mouse/display; laptops typically integrate keyboard/pointing/display while also supporting appropriate external devices.
  • Check the actual connector,signal support,cable,display input and settings rather than forcing a plug or assuming every similar socket provides video.

h.en: 2.6 SMPS,laptop adapter/battery and safe power concepts

body.en:
A desktop switched-mode power supply (SMPS) converts suitable input power into regulated outputs required by the system. It is not RAM,storage or a data connector. Laptop power commonly involves an appropriate external adapter/charging circuitry and a battery.

  • Power ratings,connector compatibility and charging protocols must match the manufacturer’s requirements. A same-shaped plug does not establish electrical compatibility.
  • Disconnect appropriate power sources before authorized internal identification;internal batteries require model-specific service instructions. Do not improvise mains/grounding connections.
  • Never open an SMPS/charger/monitor enclosure or probe mains/internal high-voltage circuitry for this unit. Hazardous stored charge may remain after unplugging;refer such work to qualified service personnel.
  • Stop if batteries are swollen,leaking,damaged or hot abnormally;do not bend,puncture,short terminals or continue using a damaged pack.
  • No voltage measurement,power-supply repair,battery removal or physical component handling is executed in this sandbox.

h.en: 3.1 Hardware versus software versus firmware

body.en:
TermMeaningExample
HardwarePhysical electronic/mechanical components.CPU package,RAM module,system board,keyboard,storage drive.
SoftwareInstructions/programs and associated data used by the system.OS,drivers,applications.
FirmwareSoftware for low-level device/platform functions,typically stored in nonvolatile memory.Platform startup firmware or device-controller firmware.

The flash chip is hardware;the firmware contents are software. Firmware may be updateable through a manufacturer-supported process,but this unit does not flash,reset or modify firmware. A driver generally operates with the OS and is not interchangeable with the device’s firmware.

h.en: 3.2 BIOS and UEFI concepts

body.en:
Legacy BIOS is rooted in older PC platform-firmware conventions. UEFI(Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) defines interfaces between platform firmware,the OS loader and suitable pre-boot services. It is not simply a prettier BIOS setup screen.

  • Firmware initializes relevant platform hardware and participates in transferring control to the OS boot process. Setup menus/features vary by manufacturer and platform.
  • UEFI supports different architectures;an example using Apple Silicon/macOS must not be assumed to have the same Windows x86 setup screens or servicing workflow.
  • Secure Boot is a related verification feature under platform policy,not proof that all software/firmware is safe. Do not disable it or change TPM/boot/security settings for this identification unit.
  • BIOS/UEFI observation is guided/read-only only. No BIOS screen is accessed,firmware version measured,setting changed or update performed here.

h.en: 3.3 CMOS,RTC battery and nonvolatile settings are not the firmware program

body.en:
CMOS names a semiconductor technology and,in traditional PC vocabulary,the small battery-backed configuration-memory context. The real-time clock (RTC) and its backup battery are related but are not the BIOS/UEFI program itself.

  • Platform firmware code commonly resides in nonvolatile flash. Modern settings may use NVRAM;not every system stores all settings in one classic battery-backed CMOS arrangement.
  • The coin-cell/RTC battery is not the laptop’s main operating battery and does not power the full RAM/SSD when a machine is switched off.
  • Removing a battery does not universally erase firmware,reset every setting or solve all faults. Procedures differ by model and can affect startup/security state.
  • No CMOS clear,jumper/password reset,battery removal or NVRAM/TPM change is assigned/executed. Follow a specific authorized service procedure only when relevant later.

h.en: 4.1 Laptop core board,memory,expansion and storage

body.en:
A laptop integrates core processing and interfaces into a portable assembly. Identify roles using the exact model/service manual rather than assuming a universal internal layout.

Syllabus componentRole / variation
CPU / system boardExecutes/control-supports processing;may be integrated rather than socket-replaceable.
Memory (RAM)Working state;may be slot-based,soldered or unified/integrated. Do not infer upgradeability from the capacity label.
Expansion slots/interfacesProvide supported extra functions where implemented;not every laptop has every desktop expansion option.
Internal storagePersistent HDD/SSD or integrated storage,depending on model.
Removable-media drive/supportOptical/removable readers may be absent,external or model-dependent;absence is not automatically a fault.
Power supply/batteryAppropriate adapter,charging circuitry and main battery support operation;not interchangeable with the RTC cell.

The supplied Apple profiles illustrate modern integration,not instructions to remove memory or storage modules. No laptop has been opened or serviced here.

h.en: 4.2 Laptop video,input,cooling,audio,camera and wireless

body.en:
Component groupFunction / caution
Video display controller/GPU and displayGenerate/drive visual output;graphics may be integrated,discrete or part of a SoC.
InputIntegrated keyboard/touchpad and supported external input interfaces.
PortsExternal physical connections;their capabilities depend on the actual implementation.
Cooling:fan/heat sink/thermal pathTransfers heat;many systems use fans,but some designs are fanless. Do not block vents or assume every model has a replaceable fan.
Speakers,webcam and microphonesAudio/video input/output;privacy,drivers and permissions can affect operation.
Wireless module:Wi-Fi/BluetoothWireless connectivity through suitable radios/antennas/OS support;may be integrated or separately serviceable.

A webcam not working may involve software permissions,not necessarily a failed physical part. A cooling diagram is a concept illustration,not a thermal measurement or instruction to dismantle a powered device.

h.en: 4.3 Front/back panels:ports and matching connectors

body.en:
A port is the device-side connection point;the connector is the matching cable/device plug arrangement. Desktop front/back and laptop-side positions vary. Use markings and the exact manual;drawn shapes here are simplified recognition aids,not electrical pinouts.

Port/connectorTypical purposeDo not assume
USB(Type-A/Type-C and other variants)Supported peripherals/data and,where implemented,appropriate power/display modes.Connector shape alone does not determine USB version,charging or video.
HDMISupported digital display/audio connection.A mechanically fitting cable guarantees every resolution/refresh feature.
RJ45-style Ethernet(8P8C)Common wired Ethernet connection.It is a telephone/RJ11 jack or that physical link proves Internet access.
3.5mm audio jackSupported headphones/speakers/microphone or combined analog role.Every jack has the same TRS/TRRS/microphone function.
VGA(DE-15)Traditional analog video connection.It carries HDMI-style digital audio/video features.
ThunderboltSupported high-speed data/video/expansion functions under the relevant standard.All same-shaped USB-C or Mini DisplayPort sockets are Thunderbolt.

Never force a connector,insert tools into contacts/vents or test an unknown power connection by trial. Inspect external labels/manufacturer documentation before connecting an appropriate device.

h.en: 4.4 USB-C versus USB/Thunderbolt capabilities

body.en:
USB-C is a connector form. USB data protocols,DisplayPort alternate modes,Power Delivery and Thunderbolt are capability/standard questions that require compatible implementations and cables—not merely that form.

  • Thunderbolt 1/2 used a Mini DisplayPort-style connector;Thunderbolt 3/4/5 use USB-C. An identical outline alone is not identification of the protocol.
  • Power Delivery is negotiated under compatible source/sink/cable capabilities. Do not infer universal charging wattage or video from a USB-C socket.
  • The actual Mac mini reference distinguishes front USB-C/USB 3 data ports from rear Thunderbolt 4(USB-C) ports;the page/support guide directs display connections to appropriate rear Thunderbolt/HDMI ports. Do not combine unlike ports into one guaranteed feature list.
  • The software exercise compares explicitly fictional USB-C profiles to show how declared video support can differ. It probes no hardware and performs no PD/cable/Thunderbolt certification.
  • Published interface rates are not measured application file-transfer performance;the complete host/cable/device/path and workload matter.

title.en: 5. Dated Specifications and Safe Practical Work

h.en: 5.1 Prepare a current specification:dated manufacturer-listed examples

body.en:
For a “latest” specification exercise,record the exact model/configuration,source and check date. The two profiles below were checked against the first/base columns of official manufacturer pages on 29 October 2026. They are dated educational references,not a claim of globally newest hardware,local stock/price,purchasing suitability,upgrade compatibility or measured performance.

FieldLaptop referenceDesktop reference
Selected configurationMacBook Air 13-inch M5,first/base columnMac mini M6,first/base column—not M5 Pro
Processor/GPUM5: 10-core CPU,8-core integrated GPUM6: 12-core CPU,12-core integrated GPU
Memory/storage16GB unified memory;512 GB SSD16GB unified memory;256GB SSD
Display13.6-inch LED-backlit IPS,2560×1664External display;no built-in panel
Ports2 Thunderbolt 4(USB-C),MagSafe3,3.5mm headphoneFront: 2 USB-C/USB 3 and 3.5mm;rear: 3 Thunderbolt 4,HDMI,2.5Gb Ethernet
Connectivity/OSWi-Fi 7,Bluetooth 6;macOSWi-Fi 7,Bluetooth 6,2.5Gb Ethernet;macOS

Platform boundary: these are Apple Silicon/macOS examples,not a Windows x86 BIOS/assembly guide. Unified-memory labels do not mean removable DIMMs. Choose your own authorized Windows/Linux/OEM system if that is your class bench,and verify its exact documentation.

The syllabus’s 13th-generation Core i5/16GB DDR4/512 GB/Windows 11 laptop is an illustrative sample,not automatically the newest configuration in October 2026. Do not mix base and upgraded columns or the largest advertised RAM/storage options into a false single model.

h.en: 5.2 Four tested software helpers and the specification worksheet

body.en:
The supporting programs are software-only,not physical practical evidence:

  • Read-only sandbox inventory: generic OS/kernel architecture,logical CPU count and exposed Linux MemTotal. These do not identify the learner’s physical laptop,installed DIMMs,ports or firmware mode.
  • Unit arithmetic:16 GiB=17,179,869,184 bytes;512 decimal GB≈476.837 GiB. This is not measured formatted capacity or proof that a real drive lost space.
  • Connector fixture: same USB-C shape can accompany different declared video support;charging remains unspecified in the fictional rows.
  • Specification completeness: verify CPU,RAM,storage,GPU,display,ports,connectivity,OS and source/date fields are filled. Completeness is not accuracy,compatibility or benchmark proof.

Use the CSV specification sheet for your own evidence. Report not observed / unknown rather than guessing. Manufacturer webpages can change;use the recorded date and update/verify sources for new work. No serial numbers,network MACs,hostnames,personal accounts or private records are needed in a shared student report.

h.en: 5.3 Practicals 1 and4:guided physical identification and safe reporting

body.en:
Practical 1: identify internal desktop components/functions. Practical 4: identify front/back-panel ports/functions. The supplied observation guides/CSV sheets are guided-only;no physical PC/laptop,BIOS screen,electrical output or component insertion/removal was actually inspected/tested here.

  • Use an owned/instructor-authorized device,its exact service manual and appropriate trained supervision. Save work,shut down and isolate the specified power sources before authorized internal work. Handle internal batteries only as the model/instructor permits.
  • Use an instructor-approved ESD-safe work area/grounding procedure;handle parts by edges and avoid touching contacts. Do not improvise connections to mains earth or powered equipment.
  • Do not open the SMPS/charger/monitor case,probe hazardous circuitry,short pins/terminals,clear firmware/passwords or change Secure Boot/TPM settings in this unit. Stop for damaged/swollen batteries or unsafe conditions.
  • Classify evidence as manufacturer documentation,read-only software observation or actual supervised physical observation. A sandbox result or schematic is not a substitute relabelled as hands-on work.
  • Assessment:theory 70+30 and practical 20+30=150. Unit 1 is 7 hours/16% syllabus weight,not guaranteed question marks. The 16 answered questions use visibly suggested 3/4/7-mark revision sizes,not official GTU papers or predictions.

References: GTU DI05007011 syllabus,2026–27, IBM history:the IBM 5150 PC (August 1981), UEFI Forum:UEFI and legacy BIOS concepts, USB-IF:USB Power Delivery and negotiated capability, Intel:Thunderbolt 4 versus USB-C (protocol versus shape), Apple:identify ports,including older/newer Thunderbolt connectors, Apple MacBook Air technical specifications (dated reference), Apple Mac mini technical specifications (dated reference), Dell:electrical/ESD safety and model-specific service-manual precautions, Dell:BIOS/CMOS/NVRAM background (concepts only;no reset procedure is assigned). Explanations and schematics are original. Manufacturer pages support stated dated examples,not an endorsement or an assertion that devices were purchased/handled.

title.en: 6. Answered Exam-Style Practice — Suggested Marks Only

h.en: Practice 1. Define a computer system and explain input,processing,storage and output.

body.en: A computer system accepts input,executes instructions on data,retains working/persistent information and produces output. Keyboard/mouse are input examples;CPU executes operations,RAM holds active workspace,HDD/SSD retain files,and a monitor presents output. Hardware,software,firmware,power and interconnection work together. The functional diagram is not a literal wiring layout and the CPU alone is not the full computer.

h.en: Practice 2. Explain PC development and distinguish the seven syllabus computer categories.

body.en: The IBM 5150 PC introduced in August 1981 was influential but not the first personal computer. Later systems grew in integration,portability and connectivity. Microcomputer is a personal microprocessor-based category;minicomputer is historical midrange/multiuser;mainframe emphasizes enterprise transactions/reliability;supercomputer targets suitable large-scale parallel computation;workstation is a professional/technical role;cloud is a remote service/deployment model;embedded computing is integrated for particular functions. These are overlapping axes,not one exclusive smallest-to-largest ladder. A modern miniPC is not automatically a historical minicomputer.

h.en: Practice 3. Draw a PC block diagram and explain the main components.

body.en: Show input→CPU processing with working memory↔persistent storage and output,with motherboard/interconnect and suitable power support. CPU includes simplified ALU/control/register roles;RAM holds active state;nonvolatile firmware/storage retain suitable code/data;controllers support I/O. Label keyboard,mouse,monitor and HDD/SSD as examples. Explain that modern integration varies and blocks may not be separate removable devices. A schematic is not actual board-location or electrical-test evidence.

h.en: Practice 4. Differentiate ALU,Control Unit and registers.

body.en: ALU performs arithmetic/logical operations;CU coordinates relevant instruction/control sequencing;registers/internal state provide fast working values within processing. Fetch/decode/execute is a simplified teaching model rather than every detail of a modern pipeline. None is a separate replaceable classroom part inside a packaged CPU. Core count,clock and brand alone are not universal performance scores.

h.en: Practice 5. Explain the motherboard and why a generic layout cannot establish upgradeability.

body.en: The motherboard/system board interconnects/supports CPU,memory,firmware,I/O,storage,power and expansion functions. A modular desktop may have visible sockets/slots;some laptops/compact systems integrate or solder components. Locations and capabilities differ by exact model/form factor. Check the specific service manual and supported parts. A generic drawing or capacity label cannot prove a module is removable/compatible or that an upgrade was performed.

h.en: Practice 6. Compare RAM,ROM/firmware storage,HDD and SSD.

body.en: Ordinary RAM is volatile active workspace. ROM/nonvolatile firmware storage retains suitable low-level code/data;modern firmware can use updateable flash. HDD stores persistent data with rotating magnetic media;SSD provides persistent solid-state storage with different interfaces/form factors. RAM capacity is not SSD capacity. SATA and NVMe are not synonyms,M.2 is not a guaranteed protocol,and RAID is an arrangement rather than an interface. No physical drive/RAM measurement is claimed by the units exercise.

h.en: Practice 7. Differentiate hardware,software and firmware with examples.

body.en: Hardware is physical components,such as a flash chip,RAM or system board. Software includes OS/drivers/apps and associated instructions/data. Firmware is software for low-level device/platform functions,typically in nonvolatile memory. A chip is hardware;its firmware contents are software. A driver is not interchangeable with device firmware. Firmware can be updateable,but no flash/reset/change is performed in this introductory unit.

h.en: Practice 8. Compare legacy BIOS and UEFI without treating UEFI as just a graphical menu.

body.en: Legacy BIOS follows older PC-firmware conventions. UEFI defines standard interfaces/tables/services between platform firmware and OS loaders/pre-boot functions across supported architectures. Implementations initialize relevant hardware and participate in booting;setup screens vary. Secure Boot is a related policy-dependent verification feature,not a guarantee of total safety. The Apple Silicon examples are not a Windows x86 setup guide. No BIOS/UEFI screen,setting update or security bypass is executed here.

h.en: Practice 9. Explain CMOS,RTC battery,firmware flash and modern settings storage.

body.en: CMOS is a semiconductor term and a traditional PC configuration-memory context. RTC and its backup battery are related to keeping time/configuration in the relevant design,not the BIOS program itself. Firmware code often resides in nonvolatile flash;modern settings may use NVRAM. The RTC coin cell is not the laptop’s operating battery and does not preserve all RAM contents. Battery removal does not universally erase firmware/reset every setting;no clear/jumper/password/TPM operation is assigned.

h.en: Practice 10. Identify the core components of a laptop and their model-dependent nature.

body.en: Cover CPU/system board,RAM,expansion support,main battery/power circuitry,video controller/GPU/display,internal storage,optional removable drives,input devices,external ports,cooling,speakers/webcam and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth. Some functions are integrated/soldered,an optical drive may be absent and some cooling designs are fanless. Do not infer replacement/upgrade paths from a generic image. Use the exact model/service manual under appropriate authorization/supervision;no physical servicing is claimed.

h.en: Practice 11. Explain laptop input/output,wireless,cooling and power precautions.

body.en: Keyboard/touchpad provide input;GPU/display and speakers/camera/microphone support I/O;Wi-Fi/Bluetooth provide relevant wireless functions. A failure may involve permissions/drivers,not necessarily broken hardware. Cooling needs suitable airflow/thermal design;do not block vents or insert objects. Use correct manufacturer power requirements and stop for unsafe/swollen batteries. Never open a PSU/charger/monitor enclosure or probe mains/high-voltage circuits for this identification lesson.

h.en: Practice 12. Compare USB,HDMI,RJ45-style Ethernet,audio,VGA and Thunderbolt ports.

body.en: USB supports implemented peripheral/data/power modes;HDMI supports appropriate digital display/audio;8P8C commonly called RJ45 serves wired Ethernet;3.5mm jacks have model-dependent analog headphone/mic roles;VGA(DE-15) is traditional analog video;Thunderbolt supports defined data/video/expansion capability. Positions and features vary. Verify the matching connector,markings,model and cable;do not force plugs or infer protocol/electrical compatibility solely from outline. Drawn shapes are recognition aids,not pinouts.

h.en: Practice 13. Explain why USB-C shape does not guarantee video,charging or Thunderbolt.

body.en: USB-C is a connector form,while USB/Thunderbolt/data,alternate display modes and negotiated Power Delivery are capability questions involving host,cable and device. Thunderbolt 1/2 used Mini DisplayPort-style connectors;3/4/5 use USB-C,so shape alone is insufficient. The fictional profile model demonstrates different declared video support with charging unspecified;it performs no port/cable/PD test. Mac mini front USB 3 and rear Thunderbolt 4 descriptions must not be mixed into a universal feature list. Published rates are not measured file-transfer results.

h.en: Practice 14. Prepare a defensible current PC/laptop specification sheet.

body.en: Record exact model/configuration and CPU,RAM/storage,GPU,display,ports,connectivity,OS,source URL/check date and evidence scope. Use current official model-specific data and appropriate authorized observations,marking unknowns rather than guessing. Do not merge base and upgrade columns. The29Oct2026 MacBook Air M5/Mac mini M6 first/base examples are dated manufacturer-listed Apple Silicon/macOS profiles,not worldwide-newest,Indian stock/price,physical-device,upgrade or benchmark guarantees. The syllabus13th-gen i5 sample is illustrative,not automatically latest.

h.en: Practice 15. Compute 16 GiB in bytes and convert 512 decimal GB to GiB.

body.en: 1 GiB=2^30=1,073,741,824 bytes,so 16 GiB=17,179,869,184 bytes.512 decimal GB=512×10^9 bytes;divide by 2^30 to obtain approximately476.837 GiB. This difference is units,not automatic proof of missing storage;formatted usable capacity also depends on filesystem/reserved areas. The calculation does not measure an installed RAM module/drive or define every manufacturer memory label.

h.en: Practice 16. State safe identification and evidence boundaries for Practicals 1 and4.

body.en: Use an owned/instructor-authorized system,its service manual and appropriate supervision. Isolate specified power sources before authorized internal work;use approved ESD handling and avoid contacts. Do not open PSU/charger/monitor cases,probe hazardous circuits,short pins,improvise mains grounding,remove unsafe batteries or change/clear firmware/security settings. Record actual component/port observations in the journal. Guided checklists,manufacturer facts,sandbox software reports and diagrams are not falsely relabelled physical practical completion.

title.en: Computed capacity units: GB is not GiB

code.en:
from hardware_lab import decimal_gb_to_gib

print("16_GiB_bytes:", 16 * 1024 ** 3)
print("512_decimal_GB_as_GiB:", round(decimal_gb_to_gib(512), 3))
print("1_TB_decimal_bytes:", 10 ** 12)
print("physical_drive_or_RAM_measured:", False)

expl.en: Real arithmetic converts a declared512-billion-byte capacity to approximately476.837GiB and16GiB to17,179,869,184 bytes. This is a units exercise, not measurement of an installed device or a guarantee of usable formatted capacity. Manufacturer memory labels and filesystem overhead must not be guessed from this calculation.

title.en: Declared USB-C profiles: shape does not determine every feature

code.en:
from hardware_lab import connector_fixture

profiles = [
    {"name": "Fictional A", "connector": "USB-C",
     "video_documented": False, "charging_documented": None},
    {"name": "Fictional B", "connector": "USB-C",
     "video_documented": True, "charging_documented": None}]
for field, value in connector_fixture(profiles).items():
    print(field + ":", value)

expl.en: Executes a logical check on two explicitly fictional specification rows, not a port probe. Both use USB-C while their declared video capability differs and charging is unspecified. This is not USB/Thunderbolt certification, cable testing, actual Power Delivery negotiation or a model-specific inference that an undocumented feature is absent.

title.en: Validate specification-sheet completeness, not hardware compatibility

code.en:
import json
from pathlib import Path
from hardware_lab import missing_spec_fields

data = json.loads((Path(__file__).resolve().parent /
                   "reference_specs.json").read_text())
for row in data["profiles"]:
    print(row["id"] + "_missing:", missing_spec_fields(row))
draft = {"model": "Unverified student draft", "processor": "Model only"}

q.en: What is a computer system?

a.en: Cooperating hardware,software/firmware and associated data/power/interconnection that accept input,process/store information and produce output.

q.en: Was the IBM 5150 the first personal computer ever?

a.en: No. Its August 1981 introduction was influential,but personal computers existed earlier.

q.en: Is a modern miniPC the same as a historical minicomputer?

a.en: No. Compact form-factor naming is different from the historical midrange/multiuser category.

q.en: Is cloud computing a single physical CPU size class?

a.en: No. It is an access/service/deployment context using underlying hardware.

q.en: Can a workstation also be a microcomputer?

a.en: Yes. The categories describe overlapping role/architecture/scale dimensions.

q.en: What is an embedded system?

a.en: Computing integrated for particular device functions;it need not resemble or run the OS of a desktop.

q.en: What does the ALU do?

a.en: Relevant arithmetic and logical operations under the instruction/control design.

q.en: What does the CU do?

a.en: Coordinates relevant instruction/control sequencing and signals.

q.en: Do more cores or GHz alone prove universally better performance?

a.en: No. Architecture,workload,memory,software and operating/thermal conditions matter.

q.en: What is the motherboard?

a.en: The main circuit board supporting/interconnecting relevant system components and interfaces.

q.en: Does every laptop have replaceable CPU/RAM modules?

a.en: No. Integration/soldering/model design varies;check the exact service specification.

q.en: How does RAM differ from SSD capacity?

a.en: RAM is active working state;SSD is persistent storage. They are different resources.

q.en: Is firmware the same as the flash chip?

a.en: No. The chip is hardware;firmware is low-level software/content stored in suitable memory.

q.en: Can modern firmware be updateable?

a.en: Yes,but this unit performs no firmware flash/reset/change.

q.en: Is UEFI just a graphical BIOS menu?

a.en: No. It specifies interfaces/services between platform firmware and OS/pre-boot components.

q.en: Does a missing sandbox EFI directory prove the physical machine uses legacy BIOS?

a.en: No. A sandbox exposes only a limited view,and no such inference/probe is used here.

q.en: Is the RTC coin cell the laptop’s main battery?

a.en: No. Their roles differ,and settings/time behaviour is model-dependent.

q.en: Does removing a battery universally erase BIOS firmware or reset every setting?

a.en: No. Firmware flash and settings storage differ;no such procedure is assigned here.

q.en: What may a laptop video controller/GPU do?

a.en: Generate/drive appropriate display output;it may be integrated,discrete or part of a SoC.

q.en: Must every laptop have an optical drive and fan?

a.en: No. Removable-media and cooling implementations are model-dependent;some are absent/external/fanless.

q.en: What do Wi-Fi/Bluetooth components provide?

a.en: Supported wireless connectivity through appropriate hardware/antennas/software.

q.en: What is a common meaning of LED monitor?

a.en: An LED-backlit LCD;not automatically a direct-emissive LED or OLED panel.

q.en: What is USB-C?

a.en: A connector form;protocol,video and charging capability must be checked separately.

q.en: Do all Thunderbolt generations use USB-C?

a.en: No. Thunderbolt 1/2 used Mini DisplayPort-style connectors;3/4/5 use USB-C.

q.en: What does RJ45-style commonly refer to on a PC?

a.en: The8P8C wired Ethernet connection,not a telephone jack.

q.en: What is VGA?

a.en: A traditional DE-15 analog video interface,not HDMI-style digital audio/video.

q.en: Does every 3.5mm jack support the same microphone/headphone combination?

a.en: No. Device wiring/role and compatible plugs vary.

q.en: What is an SMPS?

a.en: A switched-mode power supply providing appropriate regulated power outputs;not a data/storage component.

q.en: Should a learner open PSU/charger/monitor internals for identification?

a.en: No. Hazardous stored charge/high voltage and other risks require appropriate qualified service.

q.en: What does 512 decimal GB equal approximately in GiB?

a.en: 476.837 GiB by unit conversion,not a measured formatted-capacity result.

q.en: What do the four software examples actually establish?

a.en: Read-only sandbox reports,capacity arithmetic,declared connector-profile differences and spec-field completeness—not physical practical completion.

q.en: What is the limit of the dated manufacturer reference examples?

a.en: They are selected official-page base profiles checked 29 Oct2026,not globally newest/local availability,Windows servicing,upgrade or performance proof.
